transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-26 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Nina Patel (CSM), Marcus Lee (SE); Emma Ruiz (CTO), Daniel Cho (Eng Mgr), Priya Kapoor (Ops), Luis Moreno (Security)

Auto-summary / Topics (auto): Onboarding runbook, VPC peering, SAML SSO, KMS/HSM, pilot metrics, staging benchmarks, billing/quoting

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm Avery, i'll be owning the commercial side. Nina and Marcus from success + engineering are here. Emma, Daniel, Priya, Luis, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Emma: Yep thanks. we wanted to get this on the calendar to make sure the pilot doesn't stall — regulatory concerns more than tech, so security stuff matters.
[00:27] Nina: Absolutely. the goal of today is to align on scope, get network and security reqs, and agree milestones. we'll send a runbook after this.
[00:36] Daniel: For context, our use case is near-realtime anomaly detection on smart-meter streams, about 120k events/min during peak. latency target is sub-250ms 95th for single-turn inferences, cost needs to be reasonable — we can't blow the ops budget.
[00:55] Marcus: Okay great — that's super helpful. for that profile we'll probably recommend Dedicated for the pilot so you get predictable tail latency; hosted is fine for eval but we worry about noisy neighbors at that rate.
[01:10] Luis: On security we need SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and we have a mandatory HSM-backed KMS for key material. any of that supported?
[01:20] Nina: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS integrations and can show SOC2 reports. for Private deployments we can integrate with HSM in-customer-network but that'll add time. we'll put a matrix in the runbook.
[01:35] Daniel: timeline question: if we need Private with HSM, how long to stand up?
[01:41] Marcus: Private on-prem or VPC with HSM integrations usually adds 4-6 weeks on top of the Dedicated setup. Dedicated in VPC will be 1-2 weeks to provision staging.
[01:52] Emma: 4-6 weeks is tight but probably acceptable if it gets us the key control. are there fallback options?
[01:57] Avery: we can do a hybrid: start Dedicated in our hosted environment with envelope encryption and customer KMS for at-rest keys, then flip to Private/HSM in a second phase. that'll let you get perf data earlier.
[02:12] Priya: That sounds like a practical path. for pilot success we need three things: 1) perf SLOs (95th latency <250ms), 2) accuracy parity with current model >98% on labeled set, 3) auditability of data flows.
[02:29] Marcus: noted. we'll need your labeled eval set and a short prompt suite to run regression checks. also, can you share typical sequence lengths and max token sizes? for meter telemetry it's usually short, like 20-40 tokens.
[02:42] Daniel: yeah sequences are small. we'll share a traffic sample.
[02:45] [02:45] Marcus: (murmur) kay-vee cache warmup will help — if you have repeated prefixes we can cache KV to cut tail.
[02:52] Luis: on compliance, bundle of docs we need: SOC2 type II, ISO attestation, penetration test results, and details on data residency.
[03:01] Nina: we'll attach SOC2 and pen test summaries. data residency — do you have a specific region requirement?
[03:07] Emma: US-East for now, but in production we might need EU for some customers.
[03:12] Marcus: routing policy can pin to region; for the pilot we'll keep US-East.
[03:16] Daniel: Integration surface area — we want to call a Redwood REST endpoint and pass telemetry; do you have SDKs or recommended patterns?
[03:25] Nina: we have language SDKs and a lightweight HTTP call pattern in the runbook. for high throughput we recommend a streaming method or batch API depending on latency tradeoffs.
[03:36] Priya: How do you handle rate limits and burst behavior? we need predictable throttling during firmware updates when traffic spikes.
[03:44] Marcus: you can configure per-route quotas and burst windows; for Dedicated we can extend burst capacity with pre-warmed pools. we'll include recommended autoscale policy templates.
[03:54] Avery: pricing note — pilot pricing will be usage with a small reserved component for Dedicated. i'll send a draft; we can convert to committed monthly if you want after pilot.
[04:05] Emma: Please include a clear line-item for the dedicated pool and the fallback host cost. also need a PO template for our procurement team.
[04:16] Avery: will do. 
[04:18] [04:18] Daniel: Are there known competitors you see in this space we should watch for? Anthropic and internal teams, and we evaluated SageMaker endpoints earlier. what's Redwood's edge?
[04:30] Marcus: production-first tooling — observability at token level, automatic prefix caching, and routing policies. plus the rollout tools for canary and A/B and built-in fallbacks.
[04:41] Nina: and runbooks for ops teams so the handoff isn't just code.
[04:45] Priya: For the benchmark we need to see 95th latency numbers, token throughput, and cost per thousand.
[04:53] Marcus: we will run a baseline with your sample traffic and include tail latency percentiles, token cost estimate, and suggestions (quantization, batching) to hit targets.
[05:02] Luis: on encryption — all in-flight and at-rest keys must be customer-controlled. HSM is mandatory for production.
[05:09] Marcus: acknowledged. pilot can use CMK in your KMS with envelope keys; prod will be HSM in Private.
[05:17] Emma: what's a realistic pilot timeline?
[05:20] Nina: Proposed: week 0 (this week) — runbook and network checklist; week 1 — staging Dedicated provision and crew access; week 2 — ingest sample traffic and run warmup; week 3 — baseline perf and accuracy runs; week 4-5 — iterate on config and regressions; week 6-8 — production readiness and rollback plan.
[05:40] Daniel: That works. can Marcus tag the canary rollout steps in the runbook?
[05:44] Marcus: yes i'll add canary/A-B gating and suggested thresholds.
[05:48] Avery: Recap of next steps: Nina shares runbook + VPC checklist; Marcus provisions staging and schedules benchmark; Emma shares traffic sample and redacted logs; Avery sends pilot quote + PO template.
[06:02] Emma: we'll aim to get the sample and legal redlines promptly.
[06:07] Priya: quick question — if we hit a regression in quality, what's the rollback plan?
[06:12] Marcus: we'll include automatic fallback to a stable model variant and a throttled route to the previous model; runbook will have a step-by-step incident checklist.
[06:23] Luis: Also need audit hooks for every inference call, even in the pilot — timestamps and request IDs stored for 90 days.
[06:32] Nina: we'll include logging retention and export options.
[06:36] Avery: Great — thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[06:40] Emma: Thank you.
[06:42] Meeting ends.
